title: Film a live road work zone
brief:
Daylight on I-10 downtown. Film from chest height on a legal sidewalk or overpass.

- at least four cones or barrels
- a temporary sign you can actually read
- old lane paint still sitting next to the new markings

Empty cones on a quiet weekend do not count.

title: Walk through your kitchen
brief: We are collecting kitchens that look lived in, not staged. Walk slowly through yours at chest height. Show the counters, the sink, the fridge and anything on the floor. Open one drawer if you can. Messy is useful. Please keep faces out of the video.

title: Walk from the sidewalk to a front door
brief:
Park Slope. Do this in order:
1. Start on the sidewalk
2. Keep walking until the front door
3. Show the stoop or stairs plus anything sitting in the path

Delivery robots already handle flat sidewalks. This last stretch is where they get stuck. Do not just film the building from the curb.
locationName: Park Slope, New York, United States

title: Loading dock from the sidewalk
brief:
Public sidewalk only. Do not walk into the yard.

- loading bays
- any trailers
- a forklift if one happens to be there

This is the view warehouse robots get from the street. Not a tour inside the building.

title: Walk through your laundry room
brief: Hi. Please walk through your real laundry room. Show the washer, the dryer, the hamper and how little space is left to move. Tight rooms are what we need. You can open a machine door if you want. Staged empty laundry rooms are not helpful. Thanks.

title: Grocery aisle with a cart in the way
brief: Film one end of a grocery aisle where a cart or a person is blocking the shelf. Show how deep the shelf really is. If staff ask you to buy something, buy something. We are training a robot arm for indoor stores so a clean product photo of the shelf is not enough.

title: Rental scooters blocking the sidewalk
brief: If you walk past a pile of rental scooters or bikes and at least one is on its side, film how much sidewalk is left. I need at least three vehicles in the shot. A tidy docking station does not help.

title: Walk through your living room
brief:
Most home robot training is kitchens. Living rooms are where the models fail. Walk yours at chest height.

- sofa
- table
- the path between furniture
- anything on the floor

Please keep faces out of the video.

title: Warehouse aisle from a public tour
brief:
Legal viewpoint only: a public tour, a store back room you are allowed in or a marked visitor path.

Need: racks, a pallet or tote and how much room is left in the aisle.
Do not climb. Do not go onto restricted floors.
A parking lot is not this job.

title: Night work zone with temporary lights
brief: Please film a work zone after dark. We need the barrels, the temporary lights and wet or shiny asphalt if the street is still wet. Sidewalk or overpass is fine. A pretty lit building with no traffic control in the shot is not useful.
locationName: Queens Boulevard, New York, United States

title: Walk across gravel or mulch to a porch
brief:
1. Start on pavement
2. Walk across gravel or mulch
3. Finish at the front door

Wheels lose traction on that change. We do not have enough suburban examples. Stay on a path you are allowed to use.

title: Left turn where oncoming cars are hidden
brief: Find an intersection with no green arrow where a parked truck, a bus or a median hides oncoming traffic until late. Stay on the corner. Keep the traffic light in frame. If the left turn is protected by an arrow this is the wrong intersection.
locationName: Sepulveda and Venice, Los Angeles, United States

title: Ride an apartment elevator
brief:
Indoor delivery robots often fail right here.

- call the elevator
- wait for it
- film the doors
- ride one floor if you can

If anyone in the building minds, leave. We would rather have nothing than a fight with the super.

title: Open dishwasher with the rack pulled out
brief: In your kitchen, pull the dishwasher rack out. Hold the dishes or the empty tines so we can see how the rack moves. A closed stainless door tells us nothing about how a robot would load it.

title: Washer and dryer next to each other
brief:
Film both machines in one take.

- doors
- knobs
- how much floor is left around them

Stacked or side by side is fine. Open one drum so it is not just two closed white boxes.

title: Someone stepping out between parked cars
brief: From the sidewalk, catch a person actually stepping out between parked cars. Not a friend posing for you. Do not film children. Do not get close to faces. The useful part is the moment they were hidden, then they appear in the street.

title: Open fridge with shelves and door bins
brief:
Open your fridge and go slowly.

- shelves
- door bins
- the floor in front of it

Leave the food as it is. Do not put photos of faces on the door.

title: Walk indoor stairs from top to bottom
brief: Walk the stairs in your house or a walk-up you live in, top to bottom. Show the treads, the rail and a landing if there is one. Wheeled delivery cannot do stairs. We keep training as if it can.

title: Storm door and the main door together
brief: A lot of porches have a storm door plus the main door. We barely have footage of that. Film both handles, the gap between the doors and the sill. That is the whole job.

title: Pallet rack from an aisle you can enter
brief:
From a public warehouse tour, a hardware store back aisle or a similar visitor path:

- uprights
- beams
- a pallet face
- how much aisle is left

Do not step past marked lines.

title: Forklift or pallet jack in an aisle
brief: Film a forklift or pallet jack that is moving or waiting. Show how much room a person still has to walk past it. Stay on a public viewpoint. We need warehouse traffic, not a parked forklift sitting for a photo.

title: Open closet with clothes and floor
brief: Open your closet. Film the hanging clothes and the floor space that is left. It is just a tight box of clothes. That is the point. Mine is a mess which is probably useful.

title: Apartment hallway to a unit door
brief:
Walk the long hallway in your building to a unit door.

- doors along the hall
- lighting
- how much width is left

This is the last indoor stretch before a delivery. Do not film other people's apartments.

title: Broken curb ramp that would catch a wheel
brief: Walk a broken curb ramp. Show the slope, any crack, the tactile pads if they are there and the next slab. The lip is what sidewalk robots catch on. A smooth new ramp is the wrong spot.

title: Delivery van with the door open in traffic
brief: Film a delivery van with its door or ramp sitting in a live lane. Include people walking around it. Stay on the public sidewalk. An empty legal loading zone is not this job.

title: Rail crossing with gates and lights working
brief:
From the sidewalk, film a crossing while it is live.

- gates moving or already down
- lights flashing
- a vehicle stopped

Bare tracks with no gates or lights are the wrong scene.

title: New lane tape next to old paint
brief: We are studying streets that were just retaped, not freshly painted. Film the same stretch of asphalt in daylight. Old white or yellow paint should sit next to new tape. A car choosing which line to follow helps.

title: Flooded street after rain
brief: After a storm, film standing water in the actual travel lane. Deep enough that it could hide a wheel. Show the edge of the water. A puddle on someone's lawn is not what I need.

title: Stalled car with the hood or hazards on
brief: I saw a stalled car yesterday and thought of this. Film one with the hood up, a warning triangle or hazards on. It should be in a live lane or a bike lane. Show how traffic goes around it. Stay on the public sidewalk.

title: Sandwich boards blocking the sidewalk
brief: Film two or more sandwich boards sitting on the sidewalk. Show how much walking space is left. That is a real blockage. Stickers on a pole are not the same thing.

title: Package sitting on a real porch
brief:
Walk up to a porch where a package is already sitting.

- keep the box in frame
- keep the door in frame
- do not pick the package up

We need the drop-off view a delivery robot would have. Not a product shot of a box.

title: Wet or icy porch steps
brief: After rain or melt, film porch steps that are wet or icy. Show the steps, the rail and the shine. Walk them only if it is safe. If it looks dangerous use your own steps instead.

title: City work zone with a flagger
brief:
Daylight. All of this has to be in the shot:

- a live flagger
- a readable stop or slow paddle
- cones
- a truck in the closed lane

Cones sitting out with nobody working do not count.

title: Tram sharing a lane with cars
brief: We want mixed traffic. Not a tourist shot of a pretty tram. From the sidewalk film the rails, a car on or next to them and the doors if they open.

title: School bus with the stop arm out
brief: Need the stop arm or flashers out. Cars actually stopped. Keep the camera on the street and the bus. Do not point at children at all.

title: Mattress or debris in a live lane
brief: Film something big enough in a live lane that cars have to nudge around it. A mattress or similar debris. Sidewalk or overpass is fine. Trash sitting on the curb is not this.
locationName: I-5 corridor, Los Angeles, United States

title: Cyclists riding in a car lane
brief:
Daylight. Stay on the sidewalk.

- two or more bikes in a car lane
- not a painted bike lane
- a car yielding or passing
locationName: Market Street, San Francisco, United States

title: Airport pickup curb with stacked vans
brief:
Commercial arrivals curb. Stay on the public island. Do not walk in the roadway.

- buses
- hotel vans
- double parked cars
- people cutting between bumpers
locationName: LAX arrivals curb, Los Angeles, United States

title: Wet road at night with headlight glare
brief: We are missing wet roads at night. After dark, film a wet street with headlights blooming along the lanes. Sidewalk or overpass is fine. Thank you.

title: Open car door on a narrow street
brief: Car door hanging open into the travel lane or bike lane on a skinny street. Show how much room is left to get past. That is the whole thing.

title: Bulk bins in a store back aisle
brief: In a hardware store or grocery back aisle, film open totes or bulk boxes. Include a person picking from them if you catch one. Stay on the public side of the store. We need the picking motion, not a still of closed boxes.

title: Store sliding door opening and closing
brief:
Someone walking through a store sliding door.

- the open
- the close
- the lip at the floor

A still photo of the glass is not the job.

title: Revolving door making a full turn
brief: In a public lobby, film someone going through a heavy revolving door for one full rotation. A notice board next to the door is not enough.

title: Temporary walkway beside construction
brief: Walk the plywood or asphalt path beside a construction fence. Include any step or ramp. Show how much width is left. This has to be a sidewalk next to a site. A plaza with no fencing is the wrong place.

title: Shoes piled by the front door
brief: The pile of shoes by your front door. How much space is left to get inside. First indoor obstacle after the porch. Your place only.

title: Kitchen after cooking, still messy
brief: Please do not tidy first. Film the pans, the crumbs and the sink as they are. Then walk the rest of the room. We want a kitchen nobody staged. If it looks like a listing photo we will pass.

title: Busy station hall with people stopping
brief:
Grand Central concourse. Chest height.

- dense indoor flow
- luggage
- people stopping in the walking line

We are studying how a robot would move through a crowd. Stay off the tracks.
locationName: Grand Central, New York, United States

title: Walk from the hamper to the washer
brief: Start at the hamper. Walk to the washing machine. Carry the laundry if you want. The path is the task. A close-up of a washer sitting alone is not.

title: Bedroom with the bed unmade
brief:
If it fits, walk three sides of a bedroom.

- unmade bed
- leftover floor
- cables

Nobody else in the room. Try not to catch yourself in a mirror.

title: Construction gate with a truck waiting
brief: Film a site gate or fence line with a truck waiting or entering. Show how much sidewalk is left beside it. This is temporary driveway control. Not an empty fence.

title: From the garage into the house
brief: The step from your garage slab up into the house. The door. The usual mess around it. That indoor-outdoor cut is usually ugly which is fine.

title: Scaffold tunnel over the sidewalk
brief:
Walk five to ten meters through it.

- posts
- the lighting change
- how much sidewalk width is left

Midtown does this constantly. Our robots still treat it like open path.

title: Sidewalk driveway with a car pulling out
brief: Walk across two driveway cuts on the sidewalk. If a car is nosing out, include it. We need that suburban crossing. Not a pretty empty street.

title: Taxi stand with people between cars
brief:
I keep seeing this at 30th Street. We never have footage.

- stacked pickups
- bags
- people standing in the gaps

Island or sidewalk is fine.

title: Outdoor tables pushing you into the street
brief: Outdoor dining or stanchions eat the sidewalk so you have to step into the bike lane or the street. Film the walking space that is left. Then film the step out.

title: Sidewalk lifted by tree roots
brief: Find a sidewalk slab lifted high enough that a wheel would catch. Walk it. Show the lip. That is all I need.

title: Faded crosswalk that is almost gone
brief: Film a worn crosswalk where the bars are almost gone. Include the signal if there is one. Do not pick a fresh crossing just because it looks nice.

title: Manhole sitting above or below the street
brief: Film a manhole cover that sits above or below the asphalt. Get close enough that the height difference is obvious. A wheel would catch on it. Sidewalk or bike lane is fine.

title: Sidewalk squeezed to less than a meter
brief: Walk a stretch squeezed under a meter by scaffolding, dining or a truck. That narrow last bit is what I need.

title: Market stalls with no marked lanes
brief:
Walk through stalls where people cut across with no painted lanes.

- stall spacing
- cobbles if they are there
- people cutting through

We need how a robot would thread the crowd. Not a postcard of the market sign.

title: Roll-up door opening at a receiving bay
brief: From a public road or a store back you can stand on, film a roll-up door going up or down. Include the dock around it. If staff object, leave. We need the door moving. Not a closed door.

title: Parcel locker with someone using it
brief: Bank of parcel lockers from the public sidewalk. Someone using one if you can catch them. Show how much walking space is left. That handoff is what I care about.

title: Shared path with no painted divider
brief: Walk a trail or path where bikes and people share the space with no painted divider. If there is a painted line the whole way it is the wrong path. We are missing this mixed case.

title: Low awning or pipe over the sidewalk
brief: Tilt up from walking height. An awning, a pipe or something similar that drops the clearance over the sidewalk. Tall robots clip these. I never have footage of them.

title: Cable or hose across a public path
brief: Do not touch it. Film a cable or hose lying across a public path so it is obvious someone could trip. That is the obstacle.

title: Underpass where the light drops
brief:
Walk in from daylight and out the other side.

- the lighting drop
- columns
- how much width is left

The transition is what we need. Not a still standing in the dark.

title: Heavy street door someone is opening
brief: Film a heavy or revolving street door while someone is actually using it. Full open and close. An unused door sitting there tells us the weight wrong.

title: Street lamp charger on the sidewalk
brief: Charger on a lamp post or bollard. A car if one is plugged in. How much sidewalk is left around it. That is the whole thing.

title: Speed bump with the warning paint
brief: Film a speed bump or speed table. Include the warning paint on the approach. A car hitting it if you catch one. I want the approach. Not a close-up of the rubber.

title: Alley too narrow for two people
brief: Walk an alley where two people cannot pass cleanly. Show the bins. Show how much width is left.

title: Kiosk stools blocking the sidewalk
brief: Sidewalk kiosk with stools out. Show how much walking lane is left. This is an obstacle. A product photo of the kiosk alone is not enough.

title: Bags on the sidewalk forcing you into the street
brief: Trash bags or delivery bags that force you to step into the street. Film that step out. That is the hazard.

title: Wet indoor floor in a store or station
brief:
Public aisle.

- mopped or wet tile
- reflections
- a crate or cart if one is there

We have very few indoor slip cases. We need them.

title: Car pulling into a tight parking stall
brief: Film a car actually pulling into a tight stall. Show the clearance that is left. A parked car already sitting there is not the sample.

title: Stairs and a ramp at the same entrance
brief:
Find a public entrance that splits.

- library, station or hall
- stairs in the same view
- a ramp in the same view

Film both so the choice is clear. One side only is incomplete.
